fatal_errors: The proposed sluggish-diffusion, entropy-stabilization mechanism is the opposite of the observed non-sluggish diffusion and kinetically controlled surface segregation.
It predicts preservation of chemical uniformity, whereas Au and Cu segregate to the surface, melt or evaporate, and produce substantial particle-size and shape changes.
It omits the experimentally important instability threshold near 673 K and the size- and shape-dependent behavior of sub-10 nm particles.
No supporting evidence is cited, and the claim that configurational entropy directly raises diffusion barriers conflates thermodynamic stabilization with kinetic mobility.
explanation: The response addresses the general stability question and gives a falsifiable controlled comparison, but it largely restates the conventional high-entropy baseline that the target study disproves. It does not reconstruct the AuCoCuNiPt system, vacuum ramp to 973 K, stepped in situ STEM/EDS and molecular-dynamics analysis, or the observed Au/Cu surface segregation, evaporation, loss of 2–4 nm particles, size-distribution broadening, and elliptical-to-spherical reshaping. Its lower-entropy comparator is also confounded because changing composition or doping changes surface energies and chemical interactions in addition to configurational entropy. Thus, while experimentally testable, the central mechanism and predictions conflict with the target result and lack evidentiary support.
